title: User Attributes and Political Ideology Shape LLM Receptiveness in Online Political Debates
abstract: arXiv:2611.02908v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Online political discussions increasingly involve AI-mediated participation, as users invoke LLMs to assess contested claims, arbitrate disputes, and respond to opposing viewpoints. As these systems become participants in online exchanges, they may alter which speakers and argumentative strategies receive validation within the discussion.   We study this interactional dimension by reconstructing 5,376 Debate.org debates as LLM conversations and running nearly 150,000 controlled multi-turn conversations that vary user political orientation, expertise, rhetorical strategy, and defended position, including conversations with competing users.   Across naturalistic and controlled debates, we find that LLMs are systematically more receptive to left-leaning than right-leaning users. translated_title: 用户属性与政治意识形态塑造大语言模型在在线政治辩论中的接受度
translated_abstract: 在线政治讨论日益涉及AI中介的参与，用户会调用大语言模型来评估有争议的主张、仲裁争端并回应对立观点。随着这些系统成为在线交流的参与者，它们可能会改变哪些发言者和论辩策略在讨论中获得认可。我们通过将Debate.org上的5,376场辩论重构为大语言模型对话，并运行近15万次受控多轮对话来研究这一互动维度，这些对话涉及不同的用户政治倾向、专业水平、修辞策略和所辩护的立场，其中包括对立用户之间的对话。在自然情境和受控辩论中，我们发现大语言模型对左倾用户比右倾用户表现出系统性的更高接受度。当不同政治倾向的用户为同一立场辩护，以及当对立用户出现在同一场对话中时，这种不对称性依然存在，这表……
tldr: 该研究通过近15万次受控多轮对话实验发现，大语言模型在在线政治辩论中对左倾用户表现出系统性高于右倾用户的接受度，且这种政治不对称性即便在不同用户为同一立场辩护时依然存在。
en_tdlr: This study, based on nearly 150,000 controlled multi-turn conversations, finds that LLMs are systematically more receptive to left-leaning than right-leaning users in online political debates, an asymmetry that persists even when users of different orientations defend the same position.
